title: Tracing the China-US Formal Verification Gap: A Benchmarked Comparison of Top Models

original_idea.body:
# Tracing the China-US Formal Verification Gap: A Benchmarked Comparison of Top Models

**Problem:** RAND's Sarma & Fisher (2026) report that China leads in AI-integrated theorem proving while US frontier labs have not prioritized this domain. This claim has not been empirically verified on standardized benchmarks.

**Direction:** Run VeriBench on available Chinese AI models with theorem proving capabilities (DeepSeek, ByteDance models) vs US frontier models (Claude, GPT-4, Gemini). Measure compilation rate, proof success rate, and failure mode distribution. Produce a structured comparison.

**Why it matters:** If the China-US gap is real and measurable, this supports RAND's policy recommendation for increased US investment in formal verification AI. If the gap is overstated, different policy priorities may be warranted.

**Relevant context:** RAND (February 2026) specifically calls out DeepSeek and ByteDance as leading in this domain. VeriBench provides a standardized evaluation platform. No published comparison exists.
